aptitudeTests.title: Technical & Core CS Assessment 2026
aptitudeTests.instructions: This assessment evaluates fundamental Data Structures, Algorithms, and Operating Systems concepts. Answer all 5 questions within 30 minutes.

questions.questionText: What is the worst-case time complexity of QuickSort when the pivot chosen is always the extreme element in a sorted array?
questions.explanation: When an extreme element is always chosen as pivot in a sorted array, the partition yields subproblems of size 0 and n-1, producing an O(n^2) recursion depth.

questions.questionText: Which data structure is primarily used in Breadth-First Search (BFS) graph traversal?
questions.explanation: BFS explores vertices in order of distance from source, using a First-In-First-Out (FIFO) Queue.

questions.questionText: In relational database design, which normal form eliminates transitive functional dependencies?
questions.explanation: 3NF requires a table to be in 2NF and have no transitive functional dependencies of non-prime attributes on candidate keys.

questions.questionText: What HTTP status code is most appropriate when a client attempts to submit a duplicate unique application?
questions.explanation: RFC 9110 specifies 409 Conflict when a request cannot be completed due to a conflict with the current state of the target resource, such as duplicate unique constraint violation.

questions.questionText: In a distributed web system, what does the CAP theorem state regarding network partitions?

options.A: You must sacrifice both Consistency and Availability
options.B: You can achieve Consistency, Availability, and Partition Tolerance simultaneously
options.C: Under a network partition, a distributed store must choose between Consistency and Availability
options.D: Network partitions can be eliminated with redundant fiber optic links

questions.explanation: The CAP theorem states that any distributed data store can guarantee at most two of the three properties: Consistency, Availability, and Partition tolerance.

aptitudeTests.title: Quantitative & Logical Aptitude Test
aptitudeTests.instructions: Quantitative problems covering Speed, Distance, Probability, and Work. Calculators are not allowed.

questions.questionText: A train running at 72 km/hr crosses an electric pole in 15 seconds. What is the length of the train in metres?
questions.explanation: Speed = 72 * (5/18) = 20 m/s. Distance (train length) = Speed * Time = 20 * 15 = 300 metres.

questions.questionText: A and B together can do a piece of work in 12 days, while B alone can finish it in 30 days. In how many days can A alone complete the work?
If two unbiased dice are thrown simultaneously, what is the probability of obtaining a total sum of 8?
questions.explanation: Pairs with sum 8: (2,6), (3,5), (4,4), (5,3), (6,2) -> 5 outcomes out of 36. Probability = 5/36.

questions.questionText: Find the next number in the series: 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is 2x the previous term + 1: 63 * 2 + 1 = 127.
